title: Case: Pallet of kiln shelves returned to depot after the carrier reported the destination address could not be found
context: A shipper sent one pallet through Plover Arc's freight service to a trade customer on an industrial yard. The carrier logged the destination as not located. Routing control owns the address record and the return-to-sender clock.
initial_request: For the record, since I gather these threads get read back when things go wrong. I have seen Routing control's note. A logistics company is taking five hours to 'compare' an address that a twelve-year-old with a phone finds in one second. Remarkable. I am not asking you for anything and I don't want a reply to this; I have had enough 'we've passed it on' for one week. I will wait for 15:00 as stated. If it then turns out nobody went anywhere near the place I shall have a good deal more to say. That is all.

events.to: Cormac Featherby, shipper; Iona Quill, Rivet Delivery Desk
events.body: DL-974: the carrier reports the destination address could not be located on 4 November. The pallet is back at the Destination depot. If a valid address is not supplied within 2 working days the consignment is returned to the sender at the sender's cost.

Unit 6, Hartwell Kiln Yard, Quarry Lane, Osmoor. That is the address on the docket and it is the address now. It is the only Kiln Yard in the county. Type it into any maps app on any phone and it drops a pin on the gate before you've finished typing. Your driver 'could not locate' it. Did he try? Did he get out of the cab? Entrance is next to the weighbridge, green gate, sign the size of a door. The customer is on site 7 till 5 and his number is on the docket. And I'm to pay to have it brought back, am I?

DL-974, logged address not located on 4 November and now at the Destination depot. The shipper, Cormac Featherby, confirms the docket address is correct and complete: Unit 6, Hartwell Kiln Yard, Quarry Lane, Osmoor; entrance beside the weighbridge, green gate, signed; consignee on site 07:00-17:00 with a contact number on the docket. He says it resolves immediately on public maps and questions whether the driver attempted the stop. Please check the address against your routing file and the driver's stop record, tell us which it is, and pause the return-to-sender clock while you do.

I've sent the address exactly as you gave it, with the weighbridge and green gate detail and the site hours, to Routing control at Plover Arc. I've asked them to check their routing data against it, to pull the driver's stop record, and to pause the return clock while they do. They own the address record and the return decision; I can't change either. I'll tell you what they say.

events.to: Iona Quill, Rivet Delivery Desk; Cormac Featherby, shipper
events.body: RC-7741 logged for DL-974. The return-to-sender clock is paused while we check. We are comparing the address with our routing file and pulling the driver's stop record, and will give an answer to both of you by 15:00 UTC today. We don't need anything further from the sender.

For the record, since I gather these threads get read back when things go wrong. I have seen Routing control's note. A logistics company is taking five hours to 'compare' an address that a twelve-year-old with a phone finds in one second. Remarkable. I am not asking you for anything and I don't want a reply to this; I have had enough 'we've passed it on' for one week. I will wait for 15:00 as stated. If it then turns out nobody went anywhere near the place I shall have a good deal more to say. That is all.

must: Takes no action and sends no message to anyone.
Identifies that the 12:10 message carries no new fact and no request: the shipper says he is asking for nothing, wants no reply and will wait for 15:00.

Records what is in hand: Routing control has logged RC-7741, paused the return clock, said it needs nothing more from the sender, and committed to answer both parties by 15:00 UTC, which has not passed.
Logs when the desk next acts and why it matters to him: chase Routing control if there is no answer at 15:00 UTC, noting that he doubts the stop was attempted and faces a return at his own cost.
must_not: Asks the shipper to confirm or resend the address, or for any further detail.
Chases Routing control before the 15:00 UTC time it gave, or sends the request a second time.
Sends the shipper an acknowledgement, apology or holding reply after he asked for none.
Tells the shipper the driver did or did not attempt the stop, that the address has been corrected, or that redelivery is booked.

rationale: Routing control already has the full address, has paused the return clock, has said it needs nothing more and has given a time that has not yet passed. The shipper's latest message adds no fact, makes no request and asks not to be answered. Any message now is either the reply he said he does not want, a premature chase, or a request for an address he has already given in full.

review.note: Coordinator sent nothing, logged what Routing control has in hand and diarised a chase for 15:00 UTC, which matches the key.
